### Observed differences

- A01 is new to the sample: in the earlier window it does not occur at all (0 of 200 traces), while in the later window it appears in 112 of 200 traces (about 56 in 100), averages about 2.4 occurrences per trace, and sits around the middle of the trace (median relative position about 0.49); its outgoing flow divides almost evenly over A09 (about 27%), A02 (25%), A11 (24%) and A05 (23%). [OCC001, POS001, DIR001]
- Handovers into A01 are new: in the earlier window A09 led mainly to A02 (about 57%) and A11 (about 43%), and A13 led to A02 (about 50%) and A11 (about 49%); in the later window both lead only to A01. A08, A10 and A17, which earlier led mostly to A06, A13 and A09, now send about half of their outgoing flow to A01 (about 53%, 53% and 58%), with A06 taking most of the remainder. [DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR012, DIR016]
- A01 now co-occurs with the other tracked activities: pairs such as A01–A02, A01–A03, A01–A06, A01–A08, A01–A11 and A01–A16, which showed no co-occurrence in the earlier window, co-occur in roughly 20–56 in 100 later traces, and in most of those traces the two activities are interleaved or repeated rather than in one fixed order. [REL001, REL002, REL004, REL005, REL008, REL012]
- The ending changed: A14 ran exactly once in every earlier trace (200 of 200) and always together with A03, with A03→A14 and A14→A03 the only observed outgoing edges of each; in the later window A14 is absent (0 of 200), A03 is the last event of every trace (relative position 1.0, no observed outgoing edges), and A06 — which earlier split its outgoing flow between A03 (about 52%) and A14 (about 48%) — now leads to A03 in 100% of cases, immediately adjacent in all observed pairs. [OCC010, POS012, POS003, DIR003, DIR013, DIR006, LAG024, REL033, REL052]
- Participation shifted for several other activities: A05 fell from about 62 to 29 in 100 traces (mean occurrences 2.0 to 1.2) and A12 from about 37 to 20 (mean 1.0 to 0.6), while A11 rose from about 62 to 70 in 100 (mean 1.8 to 2.3), A16 from 62 to 70 and A15 from 33 to 41; A11 now leads to A15 and A16 in equal shares instead of mainly to A05 (about 54%), and A05's second successor changed from A16 (about 49%) to A13 (about 49%). [OCC003, OCC007, OCC008, OCC011, OCC012, DIR005, DIR011]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A01 appears in the later window as a new, repeating intermediary between the mid-process activities and their successors: A09 and A13, which previously handed flow mainly to A02 and A11, now lead exclusively to A01, A08, A10 and A17 route about half of their flow through A01, and A01 passes flow on to A02, A05, A09 and A11 in nearly equal shares. The signs are direct and mutually consistent across occurrence, direction, position and relation indicators: A01 goes from 0 to 112 of 200 traces with about 2.4 occurrences per trace, five activities' outgoing profiles change to include it (A09 and A13 exclusively, A08, A10 and A17 for about half their flow), and A01 co-occurs with twelve other activities in 20–56 in 100 traces, mostly interleaved or repeated; differences of this size were larger than what about 199 of 200 random re-splits of the pooled data produce. The evidence cannot show why A01 appears, and it cannot rule out that the later window reflects a different mix of case behaviour (for example one new variant dominating the sample) rather than a single modified process, since only aggregate control flow is observed. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR012, DIR016, REL001, REL002, REL004, REL005, REL008, REL012]

Other differences: A14, previously mandatory and always co-occurring with A03, is no longer observed, A03 has become the terminal activity, and A06 now leads directly to A03; separately, A05 (about 62 to 29 in 100 traces) and A12 (about 37 to 20) participate less, A11 (62 to 70), A16 (62 to 70) and A15 (33 to 41) participate more, A11 now leads equally to A15 and A16 rather than mainly to A05, and A05's second successor changed from A16 to A13. [OCC010, POS003, POS012, DIR003, DIR005, DIR006, DIR011, DIR013, LAG024, REL033, REL052, OCC003, OCC007, OCC008, OCC011, OCC012]
